name: 420Arbitration
purpose: Shared dispute case, evidence, resolver, ruling, appeal and finality coordination for 420 Integrated protocols without acquiring custody or blanket remedy execution authority.
invariants: ARB-INV-001: Every case binds a claimant, respondent, arbitration domain, originating component, originating object, claim commitment and requested-remedy commitment.
ARB-INV-002: Arbitration policy is snapshotted when a case opens so later governance changes cannot retroactively replace that case's resolver, appeal path or deadlines.
ARB-INV-003: Only the case parties may commit evidence or initiate an available appeal; evidence commitments do not make private evidence payloads public or canonical.
ARB-INV-004: Only the resolver explicitly bound to the current case round may submit a ruling.
ARB-INV-005: Each case round accepts at most one ruling and appeals are bounded by the snapshotted maximum.
ARB-INV-006: A ruling records outcome, reasoning/ruling hash, remedy commitment and optional panel commitment without directly executing custody or state changes in another protocol.
ARB-INV-007: Finalization occurs only after the appeal window closes and preserves every earlier round for auditability.
ARB-INV-008: 420Arbitration cannot directly seize funds, transfer tokens, slash validators, reverse bridge transfers, rewrite rights or override governance.
ARB-INV-009: Originating protocols may consume finalized rulings only through their own explicit authorization, accounting and state-transition rules.
ARB-INV-010: Domain policies are GovernanceTimelock-controlled, default inactive unless explicitly enabled, and may not specify an unbounded appeal count.
ARB-INV-011: Arbitration records are reconstructable from chain state/events; frontends, evidence storage providers and indexers are non-canonical.
ARB-INV-012: A finalized arbitration ruling is authoritative only for the registered dispute process it represents and is not general legal authority outside the protocol.
